subject: Missing data handling in a structural equation model

messages.author: fbe2062e5c11186d
messages.subject: Missing data handling in a structural equation model
parts:
I tried to account for missing data in my structural equation model using the procedure suggested by Richard McElreath. My implementation is, however, not working and the model is failing with the following error code: Exception thrown at line 73 (which is the likelihood): normal_log: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!. Does anyone have an idea what I may be doing wrong?

Moreover, I transformed all data (6 variables with 40 participants) into long format because I didn't know how to make l. 24-25 work otherwise. I'd prefer to keep them in wide (matrix) format, though. Do you think this is possible, and if so, how would I have to modify my code?

y_is_miss <- ifelse( is.na(y), 1 , 0 )
N_miss <- sum(y_is_miss)
y_missidx <- matrix(0L, nrow = dim(y)[1], ncol = dim(y)[2])
miss_idx <- which( is.na(y) )
y_missidx[miss_idx] <- 1:N_miss
y_is_miss <- as.vector(y_is_miss) #Convert to vector
y_missidx <- as.vector(y_missidx) #Convert to vector
y <- as.vector(y) #Convert to vector

data {
   int<lower=0> N; // number of participants
   int<lower=0> N_miss; // N_miss;
   int<lower=1> K; // number of variables
   int<lower=1> L; // number of latent variables
   vector[N*K] Y; // data
   int<lower=0,upper=1> y_is_miss[N*K];
   int<lower=0> y_missidx[N*K];
 }

 parameters{
   vector<lower=0>[K] theta; // error residual variances
   vector<lower=0>[K+L-1] lambda; //  factor loadings
   matrix[N,L] eta; // LVs
   vector[N*K] y_miss;// imputed y values
   real y_mu; //mean of y values
   real<lower=0> y_sigma; //sd of y values
 }

 transformed parameters{
   vector[N*K] y_impute;
   for (i in 1:N){
   y_impute[i] = Y[i];
      for ( g in 1:(y_is_miss[i])) {
      y_impute[i] = y_miss[y_missidx[i]];
      }
   }
 }


 model{
 
   vector[K] nu; // manifest variable intercepts
   vector[L] alpha; // latent variable intercepts
   matrix[N,K] mu; // MVs
   matrix[N,L] mu_eta; // mean of LVs
   vector[L] psi; // variances of LVs
 
   // Intercepts
   nu = rep_vector(0, K);
   alpha = rep_vector(0, L);
 
   // Factor loadings
   lambda ~ normal(0,1);
 
   // Precision
   theta ~ gamma(1,.5);
   psi = rep_vector(1,L);

   // Imputation
   y_mu ~ normal(0,1);
   y_sigma ~ normal(1,1);

   // structural equation model
 
   for (i in 1:N){
   
     mu[i,1] = nu[1]+lambda[1]*eta[i,2];
     mu[i,2] = nu[2]+lambda[2]*eta[i,2];
     mu[i,3] = nu[3]+lambda[3]*eta[i,2];
     mu[i,4] = nu[4]+lambda[4]*eta[i,2];
     mu[i,5] = nu[5]+lambda[5]*eta[i,3];
     mu[i,6] = nu[6]+lambda[6]*eta[i,3];
   
     mu_eta[i,1] = alpha[1];
     eta[i,1] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,1],psi[1]);
     mu_eta[i,2] = alpha[2] + lambda[7]*eta[i,1];
     mu_eta[i,3] = alpha[3] + lambda[8]*eta[i,1];
     eta[i,2] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,2],psi[2]);
     eta[i,3] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,3],psi[3]);
   
     for (j in 1:K){
       y_impute[i+N*(j-1)] ~ normal(mu[i,j],theta[j]);
     }
   }
 } 
 Any feedback is appreciated!
- Anna-Lena

of ~ and make sure it's defined. You can use print()
statements to help debug.

I didn't understand why you defined a local variables nu and
alpha only to assign them to 0 values that get added.

parts:
Line 73 is the likelihood: y_impute[i+N*(j-1)] ~ normal(mu[i,j],theta[j]). I defined y_impute in the transformed parameters section as "vector[N*K] y_impute;".

I set nu and alpha (which are the intercepts) to zero because I'm currently working with z-standardized variables and wanted to have an easy option to let them be estimated when I use non-standardized data. If you think this may be causing the problem, I could of course quickly get rid of them.

- Anna-Lena

it in the ~ statement.
